notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
The fire rune is smouldering...

New spells to cast, new puzzles to solve, new areas to explore and new crystal shards to find have all been added over the last couple of weeks in a series of minor updates centred around the new fire rune.  All this new content is now fully unlocked in the latest minor release (V0.14.5), and it would be great to hear your feedback to help shape the gameplay further ready for the next major release.

Please keep sending any comments and suggestions you have to feedback@runesage.com to help keep on improving the game.

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
Development work on RuneSage continues full steam ahead.  The latest update out today (V0.14.1) brings a number of burning hot performance improvements, added in-game help and various tweaks to add more sparkle to the graphics as yet more polish is layered on.

But now is not the time to bask in the rosy warm glow of success, or reflect on the embers of previous releases, but instead to look forward to a blaze of new features.
 
Speaking of which, the key next item on the roadmap is to add a new rune.  I now just need to find some inspiration to help decide which element it should be for....

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
Menus, menus, menus.  It's been a busy couple of weeks re-writing the menu system to improve not only the usability (for example, it is now much quicker and needs far fewer clicks to review any maps, runes and spells that you've previously discovered), but also the immersion (for example, the menus now use the same 3D in-game graphics as the rest of the game, rather than a old-school flat 2D menu)..

Each little tweak adds that little bit more polish that draws you into the game world.  With Virtual Reality, immersion is everything!  Please keep your feedback coming as every little comment and improvement makes the game better and better.

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
Another busy week for RuneSage with two updates (V0.10.3 & V0.10.4) focused on bringing more hints and tips to the game to help give advice on how to progress if players get stuck and show what quests there are still to be completed.  There are also a number of updates to performance and layout of the game along with a new menu option to allow you to adjust the strength of the haptic feedback.  

Please keep the feedback coming!

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes: Another week, another update!  The latest version (V0.10.2) adds a number of improvements to the mages graphics and movement along with some small new areas to explore.  It also updates the auto-calibration of graphics quality when loading to take account of the latest generation of graphics cards - in particular the 1080ti.  Please keep the feedback coming, it's hugely appreciated and every piece goes into making your game better and better for you.

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes: Another busy couple of weeks adding more and more polish to the game.  This has particularly focused on adding more detail to the world to improve the immersion - more objects, better graphics, better sounds and so on - all while maintaining, and in fact actually improving in places, the performance.  I've uploaded the latest build (as V0.10.1) to help you gain a better sense of the art direction and style RuneSage is taking - any feedback you had would be hugely appreciated and help shape the next version!

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
Just a quick update this week as V0.9.0 is now in its final phase of testing and is on track for releasing by the end of February.  

The main development effort has remained on building the atmosphere and immersion; for example, adding thunder and lightning into the storm as it approaches.  This has really helped bind the mechanics and story together into a coherent game - we can't wait to hear your feedback and incorporate any further ideas you have into making your game the best it can be.

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
As the full release draws ever closer, the next update will switch focus to improve the graphics and immersion.  At the forefront of this is completely re-doing the spell effects; more vivid runes, flashier spells, better animations for the mages and so on.  Basically, making the magic more magical...

In addition, the weather system has been completely rewritten, adding better looking clouds and introducing rain as the storm approaches.  This, together with various other tweaks and performance improvements means that RuneSage is becoming ever more immersive as we interleave the story and game mechanics into a single cohesive game.

Current expectation is that this next version (V0.9.0) will be ready before the end of February, but will keep everyone updated as the release progresses.

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
With all the game mechanics now in place, the focus for RuneSage has now turned to developing the background story which drives the RPG.  We've therefore been busy adding NPCs who give you quests, adding those quests, and coming up with rewards for completing them.  For example, we've now included a second wand as a mid-game reward allowing you to cast two spells at once - particularly helpful when exploring in the darkness of the dungeon & cellars, but also we've added further depth by developing new puzzles which require two spells at once to solve.

The release of V0.8.0 is drawing ever closer and we're currently on target for this next version going live in the first week of February.  It's been a really exciting journey so far, with much more to come.  We hope you enjoy playing RuneSage as much as we've enjoyed writing it!

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
The theme for this week has been to optimize, optimize and optimize some more.  What feels like hundreds of hours spent staring at performance profilers has really paid off and RuneSage is now running at a rock solid 90fps on all systems.  On our reference PC most scenes now render in under 5ms (thats more than 200fps), with occasional spikes up to 7 or 8ms (150fps) when loading assets from disk in the background, leaving plenty of headroom for those running older hardware.

What that means for you is that RuneSage is now a true open world game; completely seamless moving from one area to another.  As we've expanded the game world (the next version will have over double the area to explore than the current V0.7.0) this performance aspect of the game has become even more important and you'll now be able to enjoy the experience in silky smooth VR.

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
It's been a busy holiday period, so wanted to give everyone an update on the latest changes to RuneSage.  The main focus since the last release has been on increasing the number of puzzles, integrating the additional challenge areas into the main game, and starting to build a story and purpose for the lost gemstones / crystals.

It's a massive change - by far the largest patch we've done so far.  Everything however is going well, and initial playtesting of the new areas and things to do in them has been very positive.  We've got further refining of the layout and mechanics to do before releasing, but will keep you updated with an ETA for V0.8.0.  In the meantime, please do keep the suggestions coming!

notes.title: RuneSage Update
notes.notes:
Another very busy week with the focus on two major areas for the next version of RuneSage; a new rune and a huge performance increase.

[list]
[*]The Winged Rune.  We've had great fun implementing the new winged rune which contains the power of flight.  With that comes lots of new spells (levitation, tornado etc) and new puzzles which need them to be able to solve, a new gemstone to find and a couple of new Steam Achievements.
[*]Performance.  We've made some massive internal changes to RuneSage which have dramatically improved rendering performance.  We're currently looking at how best to "spend" that gain, where the most likely option will be to split it 50:50 between improving the look and feel of the game (higher resolution, better lighting etc), and lowering the minimum spec so that everyone benefits.
[/list]

Alongside these the next version will also have a bunch of other minor tweaks (for example, the ability to reset puzzles back to their starting state) and improvements to pushing the game forward.  As ever, please keep your suggestions coming!
